items.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report: trio-WES identified a novel maternally inherited COL4A1 c.4249G>C (p.Gly1417Arg) glycine substitution in the triple-helix domain. items.causalEvidenceSummary: Plasma CTSB was linked to the WMH risk score and to WMH volume in the same direction, and partially mediated the risk score's effect. A WMH GWAS locus (rs7004825) sits in cis to CTSB. Cis-pQTL/eQTL MR (gene as MR exposure) showed higher CTSB lowers WMH, extending to PVS (basal ganglia and hippocampus), FA/MD and lacunar stroke; reverse MR was null and local genetic correlation (LAVA) with WMH was significant. Colocalization did not support a shared variant for WMH and was moderate for basal ganglia PVS. CTSB was downregulated in WMH lesions on snRNA-seq.
items.sourceQuote: We observed robust and consistent results of the effect of CTSB expression on WMH volume, with all 5 sets of instruments indicating that a higher mRNA expression or protein levels of CTSB were associated with lower WMH volume (Figure 3, Table S6).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: NOTCH3 is an established monogenic cause of CADASIL. This paper adds two new clinical cases where people carrying one copy of the cysteine-altering p.Arg1231Cys variant had extensive leukoencephalopathy, strokes and early-onset dementia, even though the variant is classed as low-risk (EGFr domain 31). The evidence is case-level clinical genetics only. The paper reports no new statistical association or functional data, and the authors say functional evaluation is still needed.
items.sourceQuote: We report two cases of p.Arg1231Cys heterozygosity presenting with early-onset dementia, strokes, and extensive leukoencephalopathy.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: New heterozygous deletion (4672 bp) removing the 5' UTR and exons 1–2 (canonical start codon) of NOTCH3. It was found by MLPA and confirmed by qPCR and nanopore sequencing in a 60-year-old patient with CADASIL-like white matter changes and vascular dementia. X-CNV and CNVoyant predicted it pathogenic/likely pathogenic, and the authors consider it likely causative.

HR-EGFr variant status was an independent predictor of temporopolar WMH, which was linked to greater WMH volume, more lacunes and more disability. This is not GWAS or MR evidence.
items.sourceQuote: The prevalence of temporopolar WMH differed with the NOTCH3 risk category, being 94.7% in HR-EGFr, 54.4% in MR-EGFr, and 33.3% in LR-EGFr, compared with 31.9% in sporadic SVD without known pathogenic mutations ( Table 2 ).

items.sourceQuote: The p.R1006C mutation group exhibited a higher prevalence of apathy (φ = .34), more severe cognitive impairment, and smaller right insular volume (r = -.64) compared with p.G528C.

items.sourceQuote: In CADASIL, cysteine-altering variants in the epidermal growth factor-like repeat domains of the NOTCH3 gene lead to accumulation of Notch3 protein in the cerebral mi- crovasculature.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cause of CADASIL (cSVD with white matter lesions, lacunar infarcts and microbleeds). items.sourceQuote: The molecular analysis revealed heterozygous, pathogenic NOTCH3 mutation ( NM_000435.2 ) NM_000435.2 :c.544 C > T p.(Arg182Cys).

items.sourceQuote: In this study, we established a zebrafish model carrying the Notch3 p.C680S mutation, which successfully recapitulates key age-related features of CADASIL, including cerebrovascular dysfunction, cognitive impairment, and granular osmiophilic material (GOM).

The variant was also found in his father (who has WMH and migraine), 2 brothers and a son; three of these five carriers are asymptomatic. This is monogenic cSVD evidence from one family with no functional or GWAS data; the later large-vessel infarcts were attributed to hypereosinophilia from Kimura's disease, not to NOTCH3.

Primary brain VSMCs (R153C) and isogenic CRISPR-corrected hiPSC-VSMCs (R182C) in a 3D Vessel-on-Chip showed increased NOTCH3 ECD, contractile/morphological and cytoskeletal changes, and prolonged Ca2+ responses; gamma-secretase inhibition (DAPT) rescued these. This is direct genetic causation (monogenic) supported by experimental evidence, not MR.
items.sourceQuote: Thus, we show that pathogenic NOTCH3 variants lead to phenotypic changes in VSMCs upon interaction with ECs, which can be reversed by targeting NOTCH3 cleavage.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: This paper adds new population-level variant data on top of NOTCH3's known role in CADASIL. A genotype-first Taiwan Biobank analysis (1,134 carriers of NOTCH3 p.R544C vs 11,340 propensity-matched non-carriers) found more self-reported stroke (OR 2.23), dementia and AMD (OR 2.26) among carriers. In the hospital cohort, AMD was numerically but not significantly more common in carriers (adjusted OR 1.57, P=0.36), and retinal vessel density did not differ by AMD status among carriers. The stroke finding is general stroke from self-report, not specific to small-vessel stroke.
items.sourceQuote: The NOTCH3 R544C carriers had higher proportions of self-reported history of stroke (1.5% vs. 0.7%; P = 0.004), dementia (0.3% vs. 0.0%; P = 0.003), and family history of stroke (32.0% vs. 19.3%; P < 0.001).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: NOTCH3 is the established monogenic cause of CADASIL (cSVD with WMH, lacunar infarcts and enlarged PVS). This narrative review brings together functional evidence from mouse, zebrafish and iPSC models showing that mutant NOTCH3 disrupts the BBB, pericytes, astrocytic AQP4/glymphatic function, oligodendrocyte myelination and neurogenesis. The review reports no new primary data.
items.sourceQuote: However, imaging and pathological data reveal that WMHs can appear in asymptomatic NOTCH3 mutation carriers well before the onset of clinical stroke or overt ischemic events [ 2 , 75 , 102 ].

items.causalEvidenceSummary: C-terminal frameshift mutations in TREX1 cause RVCL-S, an autosomal dominant monogenic cSVD. This prospective longitudinal cohort of genetically confirmed TREX1 mutation carriers provides new natural history data: WMH volume and WM mean diffusivity progress with age (WMH ~31% per year), and the median age of lesion onset is about 30 years. Elevated nOEF predicts WMH and MD progression, implicating hypoxia-ischemia. The evidence is monogenic and phenotypic only; there is no GWAS, omics or MR evidence.
items.sourceQuote: It is unclear how mutations in TREX1 result in vascular dementia, but neuropathologic studies implicate chronic ischemia via arteriolar wall thickening, luminal narrowing and vessel destruction.

items.sourceQuote: The only significant finding was the correlation between WMH volume and rare NOTCH3 variants by SKAT, both with the basic model, adjusted for age, sex, and hypertension (p = 0.045), and full model, adjusted for all background factors (p = 0.027).

items.sourceQuote: They completed the genetic testing: genetic screening for hereditary cerebrovascular disorders identified a pathogenic NOTCH3 gene mutation, confirming a diagnosis of CADASIL.

items.sourceQuote: In the present study, we demonstrate a major contribution of TRIM47 to brain endothelial cell homeostasis, blood–brain barrier integrity, and cognitive function, through regulation of the antioxidant NRF2 pathway.

Patient-derived R133C VSMCs show mitochondrial dysfunction and increased pro-inflammatory gene expression, and post-mortem patient brains show neuronal fibre loss. The evidence is monogenic and functional only; there is no GWAS or MR evidence.
items.sourceQuote: Similarly, in the in vitro cultured VSMCs carrying the R133C NOTCH3 variant, respiratory complex I, II and V levels were reduced, accompanied by a reduction in basal respiration and ATP production.

No GWAS/omics/MR evidence; clinical-imaging genotype-phenotype study; no difference for microbleeds/EPVS.
items.sourceQuote: Our findings corroborate the observation that proximal CADASIL mutations are associated with more extensive WMH volume and higher lacune count, compared with distal mutations affecting EGFR 7–34.

Heterozygous pathogenic carriers had higher odds of hemorrhagic stroke after adjustment (OR 8.4), more lobar and infratentorial ICH, and more lobar microbleeds than CADASIL patients. items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cSVD gene. This paper adds new rare-variant data: trio exome sequencing found biallelic COL4A2 variants in two unrelated cases with brain small vessel disease (BSVD) or cerebrovascular defects and cortical malformations. These were a homozygous p.(Arg179Cys) variant, classified as likely benign (ACMG Class II) but predicted to destabilise the protein, and compound heterozygous c.826-1G>T and p.(Gly1426Argfs*30) variants, both likely pathogenic loss-of-function. In silico protein modelling (ThermoMPNN, Rosetta, AlphaMissense) supports a destabilising effect for Arg179Cys. This is case-level Mendelian evidence, not GWAS.
items.sourceQuote: In conclusion, our study emphasizes the critical role of biallelic COL4A2 variants in BSVD and severe brain malformations, significantly expanding the genotype and phenotype spectrum of recessive COL4A2‐related disorders.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: This paper presents new functional data on a knock-in rat carrying the Familial Danish Dementia frameshift mutation in Itm2b (encoding BRI2), together with humanized App. The model recapitulates cerebral amyloid angiopathy (ADan- and Abeta-CAA), white matter demyelination, axonal loss, microglial activation, and fibrinogen extravasation leading to motor dysfunction, mirroring human FDD cerebellar pathology. ITM2B mutations are the genetic cause of the amyloidogenic peptides (ADan/ABri) that drive this vascular amyloid pathology; evidence is experimental/animal-model, not human GWAS.
items.sourceQuote: In this study, we demonstrated that the presence of familial Danish mutation with humanized Aβ in FDD-KI rats led to prominent age-dependent increase in ADan deposition in cerebellar subpial and leptomeningeal vessels, closely mirroring the cerebellar pathology observed in FDD patients.

omicsEvidence: Experimental;NOTCH3-R545C CADASIL mice, primary cultured cerebral VSMCs, NOTCH3-R90C/R544C mutant HEK293 cell lines, SUMO1/SENP1 overexpression rescue
items.causalEvidenceSummary: NOTCH3 is the established monogenic cause of CADASIL, the most common monogenic form of cerebral small vessel disease. This paper provides new functional data via a novel NOTCH3-R545C CADASIL mouse model and mutant cell lines, showing that mutations impair VSMC survival/proliferation and reduce NOTCH3ICD SUMOylation, destabilizing NOTCH3 signaling; SUMO1 overexpression rescues the phenotype.
items.sourceQuote: In this study, we have successfully established a CADASIL mouse model carrying the arginine-to-cysteine mutation at amino acid position 545 on a C57BL/6J background (referred to as NOTCH3-R545C).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report of a 74-year-old woman with extensive confluent periventricular/deep WMH (CADASIL-like pattern) and rapidly progressive dementia carrying a novel heterozygous COL4A2 missense variant (c.940G>C; p.Gly314Arg) affecting a triple-helix glycine residue. The variant is ACMG likely pathogenic: deleterious in silico predictions and very rare in gnomAD. The authors state its causality cannot be established given incomplete penetrance and the atypical phenotype.
items.sourceQuote: Molecular analysis identified a heterozygous variant in the exon 16 of COL4A2 ( NM_001846.4 : c.940G> C ; p.Gly314Arg).

omicsEvidence: Experimental;ICH: Col4a1 allelic series mutant mice (G658D, G912V, G1038S, G1180D, S1582P), 14.1T multimodal MRI (SWI, Gd-T1WI, T2WI, FLAIR), Prussian blue and TER-119/GFAP histology
items.causalEvidenceSummary: COL4A1 is an established monogenic cSVD gene (Gould syndrome). This paper adds new functional data: in five Col4a1 mutant mouse strains, SWI-positive hemorrhagic and microbleed-like lesions appeared in every mutant strain but in no wild-type mice. Lesion burden depended on the allele and mostly affected deep grey matter. Histology confirmed iron deposits and red blood cells. No WMH-like FLAIR lesions were seen, and there is no new human genetic data.
items.sourceQuote: Overall, our study demonstrates that multimodal MRI combined with machine learning successfully identify typical cSVD lesions and heterogeneous expressivity in a Col4a1 murine allelic series in terms of anatomical changes, and lesion prevalence, number and volume.

omicsEvidence: WES/WGS;CADASIL: peripheral blood, Sanger and targeted NGS panel
items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cSVD gene (CADASIL). This paper adds new population-level variant data: 51 unique cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants were found in 155 of 1281 suspected CADASIL patients (12.1% diagnostic yield), 98.7% of them in exons 2-24. It also reports a novel compound heterozygous case (p.Arg110Cys/p.Arg1231Cys) with early-onset stroke, WMH and lacunar infarcts; clinical and radiological features did not differ between EGFr 1-6 and EGFr 7-34 groups. Targeted clinical sequencing, not a GWAS.
items.sourceQuote: This study defines the mutational spectrum of NOTCH3 variants in a large clinical CADASIL cohort, demonstrating that the majority of variants occur within exons 2-24 and that cysteine-altering variants remain the primary known genetic cause of disease in these patients.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic CADASIL gene. This paper reports a novel p.C533S mutation in a Chinese CADASIL family and shows that knocking it into human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells causes CADASIL-like pathology. The mechanism runs through VEGF/VEGFR pathway impairment, with downstream neuronal ferroptosis and glial activation.
items.sourceQuote: The NOTCH3 p.C533S hCMECs exhibited CADASIL-like pathology, characterized by a loss of tight junctions, diminished proliferative and migratory capacities, and an upregulation in pro-inflammatory cytokines.
